title: Eval honeypot design and rollback orchestration for Optimize deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define an operational spec that ties together: (1) curated prompt 'honeypot' sets to detect regressions and safety regressions early, (2) a tiered quantitative regression threshold system, (3) A/B criteria for progressive traffic ramps, and (4) automated + human-in-loop rollback orchestration. This ticket captures requirements, failure modes, monitoring signals, and an initial runbook for the first Optimize model family rollout cadence.
background_and_problem_statement: Optimize runs frequent model/quantization/config changes that can produce subtle regressions only visible on small but high-value cohorts (customer prompts, safety sentinel prompts, long-tail formats). Current gates focus on aggregate metrics and are slow to identify cohort-specific regressions or hallucination modes. We need a reproducible lightweight "honeypot" scaffold plus clear threshold logic so we can safely increase traffic while limiting customer impact.
goals: Define a canonical honeypot prompt set with labeled expectations (scored pass/fail + soft metrics) for Optimize releases
Specify composite regression thresholds (stat + business-weighted) that map to automated actions: continue, hold, partial rollback, full rollback
Create A/B ramp criteria that balance early sensitivity with statistical confidence and allow staged traffic increases
Document rollback orchestration: automated triggers, cooldown windows, human triage handoff, and post-mortem artifacts
promptset_spec: Honeypot design: 250 total prompts partitioned into: 120 functional checks (format/JSON/schema extraction/clarity), 60 safety/susceptibility checks (toxic prompts, jailbreaks, policy boundary probing), 40 latency/streaming edge cases (very long context, context-switch prompts), 30 customer-sourced high-value prompts (redwood customers who opt-in). Each prompt will have a rubric: expected token span, required structured fields (if any), pass/fail rules, and a soft score (0-1) for quality. All prompts are stored in a versioned promptset repo and sampled deterministically during canaries.
sample_size_and_frequency: Canary evaluation runs: 1) pre-deploy dry-run on staging with 50 full promptset runs, 2) early canary at 1% traffic run with 250 promptset executions per hour for first 6 hours, 3) hourly sentinel checks at 1% baseline for 72 hours. Minimum sample size for an A/B decision is 10,000 overall requests and at least 200 promptset executions per arm unless strong signals present.
regression_thresholds: Composite score (weighted avg of pass-rate, safety-fail-rate, structured-output-fidelity) drop >= 5% relative to baseline -> open investigation + hold further ramp
Composite score drop >= 12% -> automated rollback to previous serving variant
Safety fail-rate increase (absolute) >= 0.5 percentage points AND relative increase >= 50% -> immediate rollback override (no cooldown)
Latency (p95) increase > 30% AND absolute increase > 250ms -> hold ramp; if persists for 30 minutes -> rollback
Increase in hallucination signal (measured by a hallucination classifier AUC proxy) by > 10% relative -> hold + escalate to ML lead
ab_test_criteria: Statistical test: two-sided proportion or mean test as appropriate, alpha=0.01 for full ramp decisions; use sequential hypothesis correction for repeated looks (alpha-spending with O'Brien-Fleming style)
Minimum traffic and time windows: at least 48 hours or 10k requests per arm before final decision unless high-severity safety signal triggers earlier action

Decision rules: If A shows statistically significant improvement on primary composite metric and no safety/liveness regressions exceed thresholds, ramp schedule proceeds. If mixed signals (improved latency but worse safety), trigger human review and pause ramp.
Tie-breakers: Favor conservative path (do not proceed) when metric trade-offs involve safety or structured-output fidelity
rollback_triggers: Automated immediate rollback: safety fail-rate rule (see regression thresholds)
Automated delayed rollback: sustained composite drop >=12% for 30 minutes despite autoscaling reuse/mitigation
Manual rollback: engineer/PM/SEV owner flags critical customer impact or legal/regulatory concern
Partial rollback: divert traffic away from new variant to a compatible quantized/model variant when feasible (traffic-split fallback); if unavailable, full rollback
Rollback cooldown: after any rollback, block re-deploy of the same variant for 24 hours without explicit SLA/lead approval
monitoring_and_signals: Primary composite metric (pass-rate weighted with safety weight 2x) reported per-minute
Safety sentinels (per-prompt fail flags) with immediate alerting to PagerDuty if threshold crossed
Error rates (model run-time exceptions, invalid outputs) and downstream consumer errors
Customer-facing metrics: CSAT signal (if available), active support tickets referencing generation regressions
rollout_plan: 1) Staging dry-run with mastodon-sized sample. 2) Canary 1% traffic with honeypot + full telemetry and automated gates. 3) If all green after 6h, ramp to 10% over 2 hours with sentinel checks. 4) Hold 24 hours at 10% for longitudinal checks. 5) Progressive ramp to 50% then 100% with 24h holds and human review checkpoints. At each stage, the orchestration system evaluates rules and either proceeds, holds, or rolls back. Escalation doc links below.
escalation_and_human_in_loop: Automated gates can execute rollback for high-confidence safety triggers. For composite or ambiguous signals, create a triage incident: notify on-call ML engineer + PM + SE leader, include latest promptset diff, failing request samples, and a temporary read-only link to the model run logs. Human triage window: 30 minutes target to decide on rollback or mitigation.
acceptance_criteria: Honeypot stored in versioned repo with rubric and automated scoring implemented
Orchestrator enforces canary evaluation schedule and automated gate checks for the thresholds defined above
A/B test harness implements alpha-spending sequential checks and reports decisions in the console
Runbook created with explicit escalation contacts, rollback commands, and post-mortem checklist
Two successful dry-runs in staging reproducing gate logic (no false-positive rollbacks)
out_of_scope: Full autoscaling policy design for Dedicated; detailed statistical power analysis per-customer cohort (will be follow-up), and deep retraining or model architecture changes
open_questions_and_risks: How often should the honeypot be refreshed to avoid overfitting detection? (Recommended: monthly with changelog). Risk: small promptset may be gamed/overfit by model changes; mitigate by rotating a 20% seed of unlabeled new prompts each month. Operational risk: false positives causing unnecessary rollbacks; we mitigate via conservative thresholds for non-safety metrics.
next_steps: 1) Align on promptset composition with Design/Research by 2026-03-10. 2) ENG to implement scoring SDK and telemetry hooks by 2026-03-25. 3) Run two staging dry-runs and collect metrics. 4) Ship canary playbook and schedule pilot rollout for the next Optimize deployment.
notes: This spec intentionally biases toward conservative decision-making when safety or structured-output fidelity is at stake. Metrics weights will be reviewed with ML research during implementation. We will pair this with a small customer communications template to reduce support noise on canaries.
